\chapter{ChannelAttribution}
\label{\detokenize{index:module-ChannelAttribution}}\label{\detokenize{index:channelattribution}}\index{module@\spxentry{module}!ChannelAttribution@\spxentry{ChannelAttribution}}\index{ChannelAttribution@\spxentry{ChannelAttribution}!module@\spxentry{module}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Markov Model for Online Multi\sphinxhyphen{}Channel Attribution}
Advertisers use a variety of online marketing channels to reach consumers and they want to know the degree each channel contributes to their marketing success. This is called online multichannel attribution problem. In many cases, advertisers approach this problem through some simple heuristics methods that do not take into account any customer interactions and often tend to underestimate the importance of small channels in marketing contribution. This package provides a function that approaches the attribution problem in a probabilistic way. It uses a k\sphinxhyphen{}order Markov representation to identify structural correlations in the customer journey data. This would allow advertisers to give a more reliable assessment of the marketing contribution of each channel. The approach basically follows the one presented in Eva Anderl, Ingo Becker, Florian v. Wangenheim,
Jan H. Schumann (2014). Differently from them, we solved the estimation process using stochastic simulations. In this way it is also possible to take into account conversion values and their variability in the computation of the channel importance. The package also contains a function that estimates three heuristic models (first\sphinxhyphen{}touch, last\sphinxhyphen{}touch and linear\sphinxhyphen{}touch approach) for the same problem.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Find the minimum Markov Model order that gives a good representation of customers’ behaviour for data considered. It requires paths that do not lead to conversion as input. Minimum order is found maximizing a penalized area under ROC curve.

\index{install\_pro() (in module ChannelAttribution)@\spxentry{install\_pro()}\spxextra{in module ChannelAttribution}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{index:ChannelAttribution.install_pro}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ChannelAttribution.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{install\_pro}}}
{}
{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Interactive installer for ChannelAttribution Pro (Python wheel).

\sphinxAtStartPar
This helper:
\sphinxhyphen{} Prompts you for a token; if you type an email instead, it requests a token
\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
for that address and exits (so you can rerun with the token).
\end{quote}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Detects your OS/arch/Python, asks the build service for the correct wheel via HTTPS POST,
resolves the final wheel URL, and installs it with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{python \sphinxhyphen{}m pip}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sends exactly one final outcome notification to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{build\_check\_email.php}} (SUCCESS/ERROR)
with a short, client\sphinxhyphen{}trimmed info blob.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{Notes}

\sphinxAtStartPar
User interaction:
\sphinxhyphen{} On start, it asks: “Enter your ChannelAttributionPro token. If you don’t have one,
\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
enter your work/university email to request it:”
\end{quote}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you enter a valid email, the function triggers a token email and returns immediately.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you enter a non\sphinxhyphen{}empty token, the installation flow proceeds.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you enter nothing, the function prints a message and returns.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Environment detection:
\sphinxhyphen{} OS name: manylinux (Linux), macOS (macOS), Windows (Windows)
\sphinxhyphen{} OS version: Linux “2014” (ManyLinux2014), macOS “13” (amd64) or “15” (arm64), Windows “11”
\sphinxhyphen{} Architecture: amd64 (x86\_64) or arm64 (aarch64)
\sphinxhyphen{} Python: running interpreter’s major.minor (e.g., 3.11)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Network behavior:
\sphinxhyphen{} Builder request: HTTPS POST to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{https://app.channelattribution.io/genpkg/genpkg.php}}
\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{os, os\_vers, arch, lang=python, lang\_vers, replace=0, uctr=0, token\}}}.
\end{quote}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Response handling:
\sphinxhyphen{} 200 or 409 with JSON containing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"pkg"}}: direct wheel URL or a directory URL.
\sphinxhyphen{} If a directory is returned, the latest file is selected (prefers \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*.whl}}).
\sphinxhyphen{} 401 or JSON error mentioning “invalid token”: prints “Token non valid or expired…” and returns.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Installation: runs \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{python \sphinxhyphen{}m pip install \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}prefer\sphinxhyphen{}binary}} on the resolved wheel URL.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Final notification (always exactly once): POSTs to
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{https://app.channelattribution.io/genpkg/build\_check\_email.php}} with fields
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{token, action="SUCCESS"|"ERROR", info="\textless{}=8KiB compact JSON\sphinxhyphen{}like"\}}}.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Packages and proxies:
\sphinxhyphen{} Auto\sphinxhyphen{}installs \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{requests}} (and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{distro}} on Linux) into the current interpreter.
\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If not in a virtualenv, sets \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PIP\_BREAK\_SYSTEM\_PACKAGES=1}} to respect Debian/Ubuntu PEP 668.
\end{quote}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Honors standard system/proxy environment variables.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Output and errors:
\sphinxhyphen{} Prints progress and a short system report if something goes wrong (OS, distro, Python, compiler).
\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Support message includes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{info@channelattribution.io}}.
\end{quote}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
On success it prints:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{Package} \PYG{n}{installed}\PYG{o}{.} \PYG{n}{Restart} \PYG{n}{the} \PYG{n}{session} \PYG{o+ow}{and} \PYG{k}{try} \PYG{n}{to} \PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{it} \PYG{k}{with}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{ChannelAttributionPro}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}. Most error conditions are handled by printing and returning.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
May raise \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ValueError}} only if an email\sphinxhyphen{}like input is given but fails basic syntax validation.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Security notes:
\sphinxhyphen{} Sends your token to the builder and in the final notification.
\sphinxhyphen{} The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{info}} field is trimmed client\sphinxhyphen{}side (\textasciitilde{}8 KiB) and HTML\sphinxhyphen{}escaped server\sphinxhyphen{}side before emailing.
\sphinxhyphen{} No personal data is sent beyond the token and generic environment traits.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Estimate a k\sphinxhyphen{}order Markov model from customer journey data. Differently from markov\_model, this function iterates estimation until a desidered convergence is reached and enables multiprocessing.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{Data}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}) \textendash{} customer journeys.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{var\_path}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{string}}) \textendash{} column of Data containing paths.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{var\_conv}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{string}}) \textendash{} column of Data containing total conversions for each path.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{var\_value}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{string}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{default None}}) \textendash{} column of Data containing revenue for each path.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{var\_null}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{string}}) \textendash{} column of Data containing total paths that do not lead to conversion.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{order}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{int}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{default 1}}) \textendash{} Markov model order.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{nsim\_start}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{int}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{default 1e5}}) \textendash{} minimum number of simulations to be used in computation.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{max\_step}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{int}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{default None}}) \textendash{} maximum number of steps for a single simulated path. if NULL, it is the maximum number of steps found into Data.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{out\_more}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{bool}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{default False}}) \textendash{} if True, transition probabilities between channels and removal effects will be returned.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{sep}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{string}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{default "\textgreater{}"}}) \textendash{} separator between the channels.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{ncore}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{int}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{default 1}}) \textendash{} number of threads to be used in computation.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{nfold}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{int}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{default 10}}) \textendash{} how many repetitions to be used to verify if convergence has been reached at each iteration.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{seed}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{int}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{default 0}}) \textendash{} random seed. Giving this parameter the same value over different runs guarantees that results will not vary.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{conv\_par}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{double}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{default 0.05}}) \textendash{} convergence parameter for the algorithm. The estimation process ends when the percentage of variation of the results over different repetions is less than convergence parameter.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{rate\_step\_sim}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{double}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{default 0}}) \textendash{} number of simulations used at each iteration is equal to the number of simulations used at previous iteration multiplied by rate\_step\_sim.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{verbose}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{bool}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{default True}}) \textendash{} if True, additional information about process convergence will be shown.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{flg\_pro}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{bool}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{default True}}) \textendash{} if True, ChannelAttribution Pro banner is printed.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\begin{description}

(column) total\_conversions : conversions attributed to each channel
(column) total\_conversion\_value : revenues attributed to each channel

\end{description}

list of DataFrames
